newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end mixed, fronts still range bound.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end mixed, fronts still range bound.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Friday in a sluggish session, with front months losing some ground with softer cash but still bound in recent technical ranges, industry sources said.
November slipped 2.8 cents to close at $2.40 per million British thermal units. December settled 1.9 cents lower at $2.576. Most other deferreds ended steady to up 1.9 cents.

"The market feels pretty much in balance and the charts look range bound. We may just chop sideways for a while," said one Houston-based trader, noting it would take some sustained cold to fuel any break to the upside.
In the meantime, traders saw little reason for prices to break far in either direction.

Despite the weekend cold, some expected milder weather next week to pressure the cash, but others said storage owners were likely to protect stocks and stay in the spot, propping up physical prices near-term.
Chartists agreed recent ranges were intact, with November support and resistance still at $2.35 and $2.50, respectively.

Cash sources said weekend Gulf Coast prices softened a couple of cents Friday to the low-to-mid $2.30s. Midcon pipes were off more than a nickel to the low-to-mid $2.20s. New York city gate gas was quoted little changed at $2.75-2.80.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip edged up 0.1 cent to $2.206. NYMEX said 19,276 Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 24,830.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled one cent lower at $1.06, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 32 Alberta contracts traded, down from Thursday's total of 22.
NYMEX November Permian natgas finished one cent higher at $2.19, while deferreds settled unchanged but were untraded. NYMEX said 15 Permian lots changed hands versus three on Thursday.

On the KCBT, November closed one-half cent lower at $2.23, while deferreds mostly ended up by 0.1 to two cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.3 cents to 17.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 96 contracts traded, down from Thursday's total of 599.
